artworks.title: Tekemessa and Eurysakes
artworks.description: Fuseli's drawing of Tecmessa with the child Eurysaces — the son named for Ajax's broad shield. In Sophocles the doomed hero entrusts the boy and the shield before his suicide; Romantic pathos keeps mother and heir at the edge of that farewell.

popCulture.title: Ajax
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Ajax places the great shield in Eurysaces' hands and bids Tecmessa guard the child — the Salaminian heir who later rules the island and turns Teucer away.

popCulture.title: Eurysaces
popCulture.description: Son of Ajax and Tecmessa; king of Salamis and namesake of his father's shield — not the Roman baker whose tomb borrows the name.
